{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward bias.",
    "If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias or increase slope to match mean reversion.",
    "After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85.0), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply decay or smoothing to prevent overcorrection.",
    "When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive drops from 85+), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.",
    "If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early reversal (e.g., 3–5 days), reduce forecast slope or add sentiment-based lag correction.",
    "For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often misjudges volatility; use sentiment-weighted average of recent history to anchor forecast.",
    "If sentiment history shows recent reversal (e.g., 0.50–0.67 then 0.00), model often fails to adjust; apply sentiment-based correction to forecast midpoint."
  ]
}
